scenes.headline: How Audex hears and speaks through one decoder
scenes.sub: NVIDIA's unified audio-text model, built on a text MoE without losing its text scores.
scenes.say: Hi, I'm Cosmo! Audex is NVIDIA's audio-text model. It transcribes, translates, speaks and makes sound, and keeps the text smarts of the model it was built on. Here's how.

scenes.label: Boring on purpose
scenes.text: Refuse to treat audio as special: embed it into the text space on the way in, and emit it as extra vocabulary on the way out.
scenes.mark: Refuse to treat audio as special
scenes.say: The idea: don't treat audio as special. Embed it into the text space on the way in, and write it as extra vocabulary on the way out.

steps.say: Speech or sound goes through an audio encoder and small adapters, which turn it into continuous embeddings in the text space.
Those sit alongside ordinary text in one decoder: a hybrid Mamba-Transformer mixture of experts, thirty billion parameters, about three billion active.
It writes text, speech tokens or audio tokens from one extended vocabulary. Dedicated codec decoders turn those tokens back into sound.
So a task is just which tokens appear. A spoken reply is one sequence that switches from text to speech partway through.

items.say: Keep text the majority of training tokens, even while the model learns audio.
Supervised fine-tuning was studied two ways: adding one capability at a time, or everything at once.
Then reinforcement learning runs on text only, the kind the backbone already knew, so the reasoning is reinforced, not eroded.

scenes.label: on AIME 2025, scored text-only, by the model that also speaks
scenes.say: The result: ninety-one point two on AIME, text only, and a million-token context, with audio added on top.

scenes.text: Audio is additive when you refuse to make it special: embeddings in, extra vocabulary out, reinforcement where the reasoning lives.
scenes.say: Audio is additive when you refuse to make it special. Embeddings in, extra vocabulary out, and reinforcement where the reasoning lives.

recap: Audio in as embeddings in the text space
Audio out as extra tokens in one vocabulary
Mostly text data, and RL on text
scenes.say: To recap: audio in as embeddings, audio out as tokens, and training that keeps text in charge.
